#### What this PR does / why we need it:

A user deletes a PVC referenced by a running pod. After the kubelet on the node is restarted (DSW rebuild), the CSI driver unmounts all volumes for the pod, triggered by NodeUnpublishVolume and NodeUnstageVolume. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130335/commits/0f40600b3160f8ecd2739fcf79ea200d30398673 and https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/pr-logs/pull/130335/pull-kubernetes-e2e-storage-kind-disruptive/1892878133883834368 (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130335/commits/f904c6f46c0afe592f36164cc54192f122e83d75) can reproduce the issue.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130335/commits/da087777a8a14013ecc826de3a5f8a22ad99b978 allows to populate the volume to dsw volume map if the claim is stuck in the terminating state.

Actually I'm not sure about this, Is adding a terminating PVC to DSW really the best solution to this issue?

If the pvc is stuck in the terminating state due to the given finalizer, I think it is acceptable. 

1. A pod is running, deletes the pvc, and the pvc is stuck in the terminating state --> the pod is still running.
2. A pod is running, deletes the pvc, the pvc is stuck in the terminating state, restart the kubelet. --> the pod is still running.
Okay, I have no question with this if it's acceptable.

1. If the PVC status is "terminating," the scheduler will not schedule new pods.
2. When the controller deletes the finalizer, it will send a request to the API server for verification. If there is a pod dependent on the PVC, the controller will not delete the finalizer, so the PVC object will remain.
3. When filling the dsw, the kubelet will check the PVC. It is only allowed to proceed if the status is "terminating" and includes the finalizer. From a time-sequence perspective, if the check passes, it indicates that both PVC and pod currently exist in the cluster. Therefore, the controller will no longer delete the finalizer (when pod creation and PVC deletion happen simultaneously).

issue_context.title: kubelet restart during intermittent network issues unmounts volumes of running pods
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

During kubelet startup, it checks all volumes against the desired state (`desired_state_of_world_populator.go`). One of these steps is a `Get` request [on the PVC](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.28.0/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/populator/desired_state_of_world_populator.go#L487C21-L487C21). If that API call fails due to an intermittent network issue between kubelet and the API server(s), the pod is not considered to be in the list of pods to mount, leading to the [`operationExecutor` to call `UnmountVolume`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.28.0/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconciler_common.go#L166) in case of CSI-attached volumes. Although the volume will be mounted again as soon as the network issues resolves, the unmount/mount action leaves the bind mount in a broken and unrecoverable state depending on the CSI implementation (e.g. iscsi device name changed). To the user, nothing appears to be wrong as the pod is still in `Running` state. Only a manual deletion of the pod will fix it again.

We have observed this in production especially during maintenance where control-plane nodes are replaced and kubelet might not always be able to connect to the API server.

### What did you expect to happen?

I think kubelet should never call `UnmountVolume` on a running pod as it will leave the mounts in an unrecoverable state that is also not really visible to the user. The `desired_state_of_world_populator` should probably retry if it can't populate the desired state due to API server issues as it seems to make assumptions about the actual state which might be different.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

This is quite the edge-case and requires a perfect storm of a somewhat, but not completely broken connection, between kubelet and the API server plus a badly-timed restart of kubelet. If the connection to the API server is fully gone, kubelet won't get into the `desired_state_of_world_populator` routine during startup and all is fine. So naturally, it's hard to reproduce the issue. I was able to reprocuce it with a lot of luck and inserting some well timed iptables rules just after restarting kubelet but this is far from consistent. So instead I have created a small proxy with which it can be consistently reproduced and put it into [this reproducer repo](https://github.com/ctrox/kubelet-unmount-reproducer) with all the required files and steps.

1. Clone the reproducer
    ```bash
    git clone https://github.com/ctrox/kubelet-unmount-reproducer.git
    cd kubelet-unmount-reproducer
    ```
1. Create a kind cluster (`v0.20.0` with the node image `1.27.3` was used in my case)

    ```bash
    kind create cluster
    ```

1. Install a CSI driver like [`csi-driver-host-path`](https://github.com/kubernetes-csi/csi-driver-host-path/blob/master/docs/deploy-1.17-and-later.md)

    ```bash
    kubectl apply -f csi/
    ```

1. Create a PVC and a Pod that mounts it

    ```bash
    kubectl apply -f sts.yaml
    ```

1. Build, copy and run the `pvcfailproxy`

    ```bash
    GOOS=linux go build -o pvcfailproxy
    docker cp pvcfailproxy kind-control-plane:/usr/bin/
    docker exec -ti kind-control-plane pvcfailproxy
    ```

1. Modify `/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf` to use the `pvcfailproxy` and restart kubelet

    ```bash
    # in another terminal
    docker exec -ti kind-control-plane sed -i 's/kind-control-plane:6443/kind-control-plane:8443/g' /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf
    docker exec -ti kind-control-plane systemctl restart kubelet
    ```

1. Observe the kubelet log if it contains the expected error and unmount operation

    ```bash
    docker exec -ti kind-control-plane journalctl -fu kubelet
    ```

    ```bash
    desired_state_of_world_populator.go:295] "Error processing volume" err="error processing PVC default/data-web-0: failed to fetch PV pvc-8308a5fc-c8b2-42c2-8f1c-c0183ea2bce5 from API server ...
    reconciler_common.go:172] "operationExecutor.UnmountVolume started for volume \"pvc-8308a5fc-c8b2-42c2-8f1c-c0183ea2bce5\"
    ```

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

The issue was reproduced on a number of kubelet versions up to `1.28.0`. The API server version does not seem to be relevant.

comments: I ran into same issue, can anyone tell me, why this unmount/mount operation will lead to a broken bind mount point ? Thanks.

> can anyone tell me, why this unmount/mount operation will lead to a broken bind mount point ?

Not completely sure but at least what I can see with an iscsi driver, the following happens:

* on attachment the iSCSI device gets a letter say `/dev/sde`
* on the host I can see the following mount: `sde       8:64   0    1G  0 disk  /var/lib/kubelet/pods/218e5b93-ad10-4c16-a01e-abe5eab43e3b/volumes/kubernetes.io~csi/pvc-e19ba943-9224-40fc-9ea6-6b5766bc03db/mount`
* in the mounts of the container (`cat /proc/<container pid>/mounts`) I see `/dev/sde /data ext4 rw,seclabel,relatime,stripe=256 0 0`
* `NodeUnpublishVolume` is called by kubelet, the mount point on the host is gone and the iSCSI device is detached
* The mount in the container process is still there (pointing to the removed `/dev/sde`)
* `NodePublishVolume` is called by kubelet, the iSCSI attachment gets the letter `/dev/sdf` now as `/dev/sde` is still in use by the leftover mount
* The mount in the container is still pointing to `/dev/sde` so far I have not been able to repair the mount even with manual commands within the containers mount namespace
Is there anything which can be done to fix this issue? What is the reason the pod volumes are unmounted on error of the PVC retrieval? Couldn't it be ignored if that happens?

After kubelet restart, volumeManger will reconstruct DSW and ASW, it already has a unreliable constraints that ASW should be reconstructed after DSW. But even if DSW recontructed failed, failed to add some volume in using, ASW will start to reconstruct. 
After ASW reconstructed, reconciler will find some volume in ASW and not in DSW, which will lead to an umount operation. 
I am thinking to add some more reliable constriants during reconstruct DSW, like never start to reconcile before DSW was fully constructed.
I ran into same issue, kubelet start container but pv is unmount kubelet log:

I also ran into the same issue. In my case, the corresponding Persistent Volume had `ReclaimPolicy` `Delete` which led to the loss of the Persistent Volume when the container was terminated. 
Perhaps someone with a deeper understanding of how the kubelet works could verify that this issue indeed leads to the loss of the Persistent Volume when its `ReclaimPolicy` is `Delete`?

I'm using AWS EKS and dynamically provisioned Persistent Volumes with the AWS EBS CSI driver.

Thanks @ctrox and @jinxycandotailwhip for a detailed analysis and a reproducer. While this issue has been acknowledged as a real issue, we still need a volunteer to fix this issue.

Basically, `desiredStateOfWorldPopulator` marks itself as fully populated (`hasAddedPods = true`) even though it was not able to read some PVs/PVCs used by running pods and put them into DesiredStateOfWorld (DSW). This is bad.

We can fix the populator not to mark itself as populated until it's able to read all PVs/PVCs. Then, what if such a PV/PVC was already deleted from the API server, yet there is a running Pod that uses them? There is nothing that kubelet could put into DSW. Should the reconciler unmount volumes only when they're not in DSW *and they're not used by running Pods*? ASW has UID of the pod for which a volume was mounted and the reconciler could check if it still exists.

@jingxu97 @msau42 what do you think?
I would be up for giving this a try once there is consensus here on how to handle the "not found" case :+1:

> Should the reconciler unmount volumes only when they're not in DSW _and they're not used by running Pods_?

+1 , by adding a safe guard on the reconciler side in order to check  that all containers in the pod have been  terminated ( [like the desired_state_of_world_populator](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6be1530bbc77d453e1d0ba387ead559de435550b/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/populator/desired_state_of_world_populator.go#L232)  .

review_comments:
If the kubelet get a terminating PVC and it has PVCProtectionFinalizer, it means that the pvc can not be deleted by the controller, because the controller will ask APIServer whether there is a Pod using it before removing the PVCProtectionFinalizer. So, it is safe to add this check in the kubelet.

If the `pvc_protection` controller or `StorageObjectInUseProtection` is disabled, there is no any difference between the current behavior and the new behavior.

> If the kubelet get a terminating PVC and it has PVCProtectionFinalizer, it means that the pvc can not be deleted by the controller, because the controller will ask APIServer whether there is a Pod using it before removing the PVCProtectionFinalizer. So, it is safe to add this check in the kubelet.

This should be a comment in the code, for future people who will wonder why is there such a check
